items.text: Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, on Nov 19. Xi chaired the session, which ran more than an hour (Breitbart says about 90 minutes). It ended in a four-point 'peace declaration', published in English by Chinese state media. In it the three powers commit to UN reform, to raising production and supply of refined petroleum products and keeping energy flows stable, to stressing state immunity and warning the ICC and similar courts not to overreach, and to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. The declaration repeats that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Al Jazeera reports that Trump said Xi agreed the Strait of Hormuz must stay open and Iran must not get a nuclear weapon. A separate Trump–Putin meeting earlier in the day centred on Ukraine. Zelenskyy called his exclusion a 'huge mistake' (Epoch Times). Trump left for Washington about an hour after the trilateral ended.
items.notes: Breitbart notes the text was released by Chinese and Russian state media, not by an official US source, so wording of the US version is unconfirmed. No details found on Trump–Xi bilateral trade/chip outcomes (search budget exhausted). CNBC headline also reports pledge to boost oil production and revamp the UN.

items.text: Anthropic (ANT) began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov 19. The first trade, set in Nasdaq's IPO cross at 11:48 a.m. ET, was $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, and the stock touched $114.99. It fell below $100 within about 20 minutes, hit a low of $92.72, and closed at $97.17, up 17.1% on the day, with about 832 million shares traded (Stock Titan). Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the opening bell. In remarks reported by Fox News, Dario Amodei acknowledged the technology's real risks, including misuse and loss of control. The offering raised about $81.3 billion, the largest US IPO on record, and underwriters have until Dec 18 to exercise an option on 147 million more shares.
items.reporter: James Cirrone, Stephen Sorace (Fox); Stock Titan Editorial Team
items.thread: Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations
items.notes: Reuters (via Investing.com) said valuation briefly topped $2 trillion at the open. AP (Stan Choe) confirms the $97.17 close.

items.text: The S&P 500 fell 2% (147.80 points) to 7,175.83 on Nov 19, its sixth straight loss and its longest losing streak in about two and a half years, according to AP. The index is now 8.2% below last month's record. The Dow lost 1,101.11 points (2.2%) to 49,097.06 and the Nasdaq fell 2.3% to 23,879.20, with more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks lower. AP and Reuters cite AI-bubble worries that Anthropic's debut failed to ease, high interest rates, regulatory risk after Democratic midterm gains, and the Nvidia leadership turmoil. Nvidia gave up an early 4.7% gain to close down 3.3%. Reuters notes CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December rate hike at about 94%. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 5.04% as investors sought safety.
items.notes: The Reuters story on Investing.com was written before the close and shows smaller intraday losses (Dow -1.79%, S&P -1.54%). AP's closing figures are used here; Yahoo Finance's closing numbers match AP.

items.text: On Nov 19 the Senate voted 48-51 against a House-adopted concurrent resolution directing Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran. It was the first war-powers vote since the midterms. Republicans Collins, Murkowski and Paul voted yes. Democrat Fetterman voted no, and Republican Thom Tillis, who had backed an earlier attempt, also voted no, saying the measure would not reach the president and amounted to a statement. CBS notes the vote was largely symbolic because concurrent resolutions are not presented to the president. Stars and Stripes reports Democrats plan to push further resolutions and to use appropriations and defence-funding limits once they take control of Congress in January.
items.reporter: Kaia Hubbard (CBS); Svetlana Shkolnikova (Stars and Stripes)
items.notes: Linked to the Dec 11 funding fight (W-261105-03). The House adopted its version in September, 220-204.

items.text: Late on Nov 18 the Ninth Circuit extended its stay of Judge Edward Chen's order restoring Venezuelan Temporary Protected Status, hours after the Justice Department filed its third emergency application to the Supreme Court. The stay now runs until seven days after the appeals court issues its merits ruling, rather than expiring Nov 20. On Nov 19 Solicitor General D. John Sauer withdrew the Supreme Court application (No. 26A714) in a letter saying the deadline no longer applied, and added that the government would return immediately if the merits ruling went against it. The TPS terminations therefore stay in effect and no work authorisation has been restored. AP reports federal attorneys put about 1,800 Venezuelans in detention and about 330 in deportation proceedings.
items.notes: The SG letter is on the Supreme Court docket. The SCOTUSblog headline was updated to 'withdraws', but the cached body predates the withdrawal. The AP story (Spectrum News) could not be fetched, so the detention figures are relayed second-hand.

items.text: In a Fox News interview aired from China, Trump called the preliminary Iran agreement 'a waste of time', said he wants a lasting deal that would bind a future president, and said the US would 'see what happens after January 1st', without explaining the date. He also said Washington is in contact with Tehran and denied that Vance had been pulled off the Iran talks. A Pentagon official put the war's cost at $48.3 billion as of Nov 13, about 26% above the CBO's $38 billion estimate as of Aug 1 and excluding base damage. On Nov 18 CENTCOM warned that ships taking cargo at sea from vessels loaded in Iran could be treated as blockade violators and face seizure or force. Iran's military claimed three tankers hit mines east of Hormuz, a claim not independently confirmed. Israeli outlet Mako reports Trump is still weighing a joint US–Israel strike, with any decision after his Asia trip.
items.reporter: Gulf News live team (Surabhi Vasundharadevi et al.)
items.notes: A Kerala Kaumudi summary says Trump would assess after 2027. The Fox wording says after January 1. Gulf News mentions a third US carrier group (USS Theodore Roosevelt) arriving in CENTCOM, which CENTCOM calls a scheduled deployment. The mine claim comes from Iran only.

items.text: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips was published in the Federal Register on Nov 19 (doc. 2026-23529), after being released on Nov 16. It requires a licence to export or transfer advanced chips to any data centre worldwide that gives companies headquartered in China, Macau or other D:5 countries access to more than 12 million aggregate TPP of computing power. The rule also covers access through intermediaries and requires know-your-customer checks on ownership. It adds licence requirements for advanced-chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, except for US-headquartered users who file monthly reports. It formally rescinds the never-enforced Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. Data centres already serving covered firms have 90 days from the effective date to obtain a licence.
items.outlet: Bureau of Industry and Security / Unite.AI
items.notes: Effective date and comment deadline not verified: the Federal Register page was not reachable (robots-blocked). SCMP coverage notes the impact on Southeast Asian data centres. The rule came days before the Trump–Xi meeting.

items.text: The HHS Office for Civil Rights has finalised changes to the HIPAA Privacy Rule, and the final rule is on Federal Register public inspection (doc. 2026-23429). Covered entities will have 15 calendar days instead of 30 to answer patients' requests for their records, with one extension of up to 30 days. Patients will be able to get records through personal health apps where providers can support it. Free copies will be required more often and fees will need advance notice. Health plans and providers may share information for care coordination, including with social-service and community organisations. The requirement to seek written acknowledgment of privacy notices is dropped. Provisions take effect 60 days after publication, and compliance is due 180 days after that.
items.notes: Announced around Nov 16-17 (Healio dated Nov 17) and not previously logged. The exact Federal Register publication date was not confirmed.

items.text: US District Judge Christopher Cooper heard more than two hours of argument on Nov 19 on the administration's request to dissolve his injunction blocking a two-year closure of the Kennedy Center for renovation. The suit was brought by Rep. Joyce Beatty. DOJ argued the board fixed the procedural defects Cooper identified in May, including through a September revote, and cited safety hazards. The plaintiffs called the review a sham meant to justify a decision already taken. Cooper questioned both sides on the two-year versus four-year renovation options and set no timeline for ruling. His separate order barring renaming the centre for Trump is not at issue.
items.notes: Single trade outlet relaying MS Now. The Kennedy Center Honors move to Capital One Arena on Dec 7.

items.text: Walmart reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $188.8 billion, above the roughly $187.2 billion expected, and adjusted EPS of $0.65 against $0.64 expected. US same-store sales rose 2.9% and e-commerce grew 17%. The company raised its full-year outlook, and CEO John Furner described the results as strong. The retailer's figures are a gauge of US consumer spending going into the holiday season.
items.notes: Only Yahoo's live blog was read. Walmart's own release was not checked.

items.text: JPMorgan Chase said some third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack that may have exposed customer names and email addresses. The bank said its own services were not disrupted. The incident follows a run of high-profile US outages, including the FAA ground stop and the NSANet disruption, though no link has been suggested.
items.notes: Single source, not cross-checked with JPMorgan or wires because the search budget ran out.
